subject: Request: DynamoPay SLA-tier routing + tenant-cache isolation (priority ask)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: DynamoPay SLA-tier routing + tenant-cache isolation (priority ask)

Team —

Short version: DynamoPay (large regional fintech, see MAP attached) has signaled final approval contingent on two platform assurances: 1) guaranteed routing that pins "priority" traffic to a high-SLO lane (95th < 150ms for critical flows) and 2) tenant-level KV-cache isolation (soft isolation acceptable as an MVP) for redaction/PII concerns. They want these in place for go-live.

Why this is urgent: Sales is tracking a $1.2M ARR commitment (deal DY-2027-042), close target 2027-05-27. Procurement will pause signature if we can’t provide a clear timeline for delivery or a gated MAP. We need a go/no-go on prioritization by EOD 2027-05-14 to avoid pushing the close into Q3.

Ask: Can Product + Eng evaluate whether routing + soft KV namespaces can be delivered as an MVP inside the next 3 sprints (or give an estimate), and whether we can ship routing alone earlier as a partial mitigation?

Attached: DynamoPay_MVP_requirements_v2.pdf (customer asks) and DynamoPay_MAP_20270511.xlsx (mutual action plan + key dates).

Key constraints from the customer (excerpt):
- Data residency: US-only processing for primary lane.
- Isolation: tenant-level cache separation; they will accept namespace-level logical separation as interim.
- SLA: priority path must have guaranteed scheduling to reduce tail latency (95th pct target).

Next steps I propose: Product/Eng assessment + rough ETA by 5/12; internal decision on reallocation by 5/14; commit in MAP to phased delivery (routing day 1, soft isolation in week 3).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DynamoPay SLA-tier routing + tenant-cache isolation (priority ask)

Thanks for the context, Rishi — and for the MAP. A few clarifying q's that will determine scope and ETA: 

1) Must-haves vs nice-to-haves: Is the tenant-level strict isolation a hard requirement for signature, or will DynamoPay accept the logical namespace (soft isolation) for initial delivery? You mentioned they "will accept namespace-level logical separation as interim" — can procurement confirm in writing?

2) Traffic profile: please send a small sample of expected QPS and typical sequence length for the priority flows (we need to size scheduling and batching changes).

3) Fallback: Is the customer okay with a fallback to a quantized-compatible model variant for the priority lane if latency spikes?

4) Compliance hooks: do they need any new audit/event hooks (traceability for cache evictions, KV access logs) beyond our standard telemetry? If so, list exact artifacts needed for procurement/legal.

Initial take: Routing by SLA-tier is mostly product/config work; engineering will need to add priority queueing and ensure batching doesn't mix priority/non-priority traffic. KV namespace separation for cache is trickier — we can do logical namespaces quickly, but hard isolation (separate cache instances or tenant-specific residency) is higher effort and may require infra capacity commitments.

Markus — can you ballpark an effort for: (A) priority routing + scheduling + batch isolation for 95th-targeted lane, and (B) logical KV namespaces vs strict isolation? If we can get (A) in 2-3 sprints and (B) as phased work, we can propose a staged MAP.

Rishi — please push the procurement/technical contact (Emma) to confirm the acceptance of phased approach and share the traffic profile by EOD 5/12.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Cole <emma.cole@dynamopay.com>, DynamoPay Procurement <procurement@dynamopay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DynamoPay SLA-tier routing + tenant-cache isolation (priority ask)

Laura — thanks. Quick answers inline and attached updated MAP (v2).

1) Procurement note: Emma confirmed (in meeting and in the updated MAP) that DynamoPay will accept a phased delivery: routing + priority lane on Day 1 and logical KV namespace isolation as an interim step. They would like firm dates and a rollback/fallback plan documented before signature.

2) Traffic profile: attached sample: priority flows ~120 QPS peak; median seq len ~220 tokens; bursty batch shapes during settlement windows. They call out ~70% of traffic hitting the priority lanes during 02:00–04:00 PDT.

3) Fallback: DynamoPay is open to model-variant fallback as long as latency/read latency guarantees are preserved and quality degradation is documented.

4) Compliance hooks: they requested retention windows and eviction logs for cache keys used in priority lane. For procurement, they asked for a short statement in the MAP that we can ship logical namespaces and that strict isolation is an available paid upgrade for Dedicated.

Deal context: ARR $1.2M; legal review in parallel; procurement wants a shipping plan as a condition of signature. HubSpot with notes: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567890/DY-2027-042

I can coordinate a short sync with Emma if that helps. We need your ETA by 5/14 morning to present to leadership and the customer.

Attachments: DynamoPay_MVP_requirements_v2.pdf, DynamoPay_MAP_20270511.xlsx

— Rishi

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DynamoPay SLA-tier routing + tenant-cache isolation (priority ask)

Thanks for the context and the traffic sample — that helps. High-level engineering assessment: 

A) Priority routing + scheduling + batch isolation (MVP): feasible as an incremental change. Approach: tag incoming requests for DynamoPay priority lane, route to a logically prioritized queue, and ensure the batching layer can create priority-only batches (no mixing). This avoids cross-tenant latency bleed. Estimated effort: ~6 engineer-weeks (2 backend infra engineers + 1 infra qa) to implement, test, and run load validation. With reallocation we could aim to deliver a safe MVP in ~3 sprints.

B) KV cache isolation: logical namespaces (separate keyspace and eviction logs) — low effort: ~1.5 engineer-weeks. Strict physical isolation (separate cache instances / dedicated residency) — high effort: ~10+ engineer-weeks plus capacity planning and possible Dedicated offering gating.

Compliance hooks: we can add eviction/access logs for the namespace with retention controls; low-medium effort.

Proposed compromise to meet dates: approve reallocation of two infra engineers for three sprints to deliver routing + logical namespace + auditing (MVP). We will flag strict isolation as a paid upgrade for Dedicated; provide a clear path and ETA in the MAP. Deliverables / milestones:
- Sprint 1 (design + routing prototype) — 2 weeks
- Sprint 2 (batch isolation + priority queues) — 3 weeks
- Sprint 3 (testing, telemetry, audit hooks, docs) — 2 weeks

Total ~7 weeks end-to-end if staffed as above; accelerated to ~5 weeks with overtime and parallel QA.

Constraints: this will push other infra work; need org approval from Eng PM to shift staffing. If Product wants an earlier ship (routing-only) we can scope that to a 3-week fast-path but without audit logs or full telemetry.

Next step: Laura — if Product signs off on staffing tradeoffs and MAP phrasing, we can lock dates and I’ll send a short tech-commitment note to include in procurement pack. Rishi — we’ll need the procurement confirmation in writing by 5/14 to prioritize.

— Markus
